title: Clinical Outcome Study (COS) on the extent of pain reduction after radiofrequency denervation (RN) compared to endoscopic denervation (EN) of lumbar facet joints
summary: This study investigates treatment options for long-lasting low back pain. With increasing age, vertebral joints can stiffen naturally, which in many cases leads to pain. Often, the treatment involves temporarily deactivating the supplying pain nerves. This deactivation can take place via heating of the nerve. There are two different methods of recognizing or finding the nerve. Either with the help of a camera as part of an open operation or with the help of an X-ray machine. This study compares these two methods and aims to determine which is more effective in reducing pain. Various questionnaires are filled out before the procedure and 3, 6, 12 and 24 months after the procedure. Participants are people over the age of 18 with long-term back pain. The study aims to show that endoscopic denervation provides longer-term pain relief than radiofrequency denervation.

interventions.name: Patients with diagnostically proven and symptomatic spondylarthrosis are treated with an endoscopic facet denervation and then preoperatively and 3, 6, 12 and 24 months postoperatively, the patients fill out three questionnaires (Oswestry Disability Index, Numerical Analogue Scale, Range of Motion).
